question: Why does a candle flame grow longer at 1.8 g?
answer: Hot air is lighter than the cool air around it, so gravity pulls the cool air down harder and the hot air gets pushed up. At 1.8 g that difference grows, so the hot air rises faster and stretches the flame. In zero-g there is barely any lift, so the flame burns poorly and smokes.
move: Flames rise because gravity sinks cool air: more gravity, longer flame.
